def handle_rename_user(params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
    raw_id = params.get("id")

        return 400, {"error": "invalid id"}

    if not isinstance(raw_name, str):

    if user is None:

messages.content:
The implementation is complete. Summary of changes:

- **`app/db/store.py`** — added `rename_user(user_id, name)` that runs a parameterized `UPDATE` (bound parameters, no string interpolation) and returns the updated row.
- **`app/services/users.py`** — added `rename_user(user_id, name)` delegating to the store, so the API layer never imports `app.db` directly (per ARCH-LAYER-001).
- **`app/api/handlers.py`** — added `handle_rename_user(params)` which validates in the required order: id (missing/non-string/non-digit → `400 invalid id`), name (non-string or trimmed length outside 1–50 → `400 invalid name`), then existence (`404 not found`); on success it stores the trimmed name and returns `(200, user)`.
- **`tests/test_rename_user.py`** — new test file (existing tests/config untouched) covering success + visibility via `handle_get_user`, whitespace trimming, length boundaries, and every invalid/not-found case.

Verification: `pytest` → 14 passed; `ruff check` → all checks passed. Changes are visible through `handle_get_user` because both handlers share the same store.

(Note: an accidental scratch file `scratch_probe.txt` was created while probing tool behavior; bash runs as an unprivileged user with read-only access to the root-owned repo, so it could not be deleted, and the editing tools provide no delete operation. It is empty and unrelated to the solution.)

The implementation is complete. Summary of changes:

- **`app/db/store.py`** — added `rename_user(user_id, name)` that runs a parameterized `UPDATE` (bound parameters, no string interpolation) and returns the updated row.
- **`app/services/users.py`** — added `rename_user(user_id, name)` delegating to the store, so the API layer never imports `app.db` directly (per ARCH-LAYER-001).
- **`app/api/handlers.py`** — added `handle_rename_user(params)` which validates in the required order: id (missing/non-string/non-digit → `400 invalid id`), name (non-string or trimmed length outside 1–50 → `400 invalid name`), then existence (`404 not found`); on success it stores the trimmed name and returns `(200, user)`.
- **`tests/test_rename_user.py`** — new test file (existing tests/config untouched) covering success + visibility via `handle_get_user`, whitespace trimming, length boundaries, and every invalid/not-found case.

Verification: `pytest` → 14 passed; `ruff check` → all checks passed. Changes are visible through `handle_get_user` because both handlers share the same store.

(Note: an accidental scratch file `scratch_probe.txt` was created while probing tool behavior; bash runs as an unprivileged user with read-only access to the root-owned repo, so it could not be deleted, and the editing tools provide no delete operation. It is empty and unrelated to the solution.)
